Beta 12.2
The Atlas, Finished
- Snow drifts down over the map in winter and leaves blow across it in autumn; mountains rise in shaded relief and throw their shadows across the plains below; rivers start as fine lines in the hills and swell as streams join them on the way to the sea; pine woods grow in the north and under the mountains
- Seas, lakes and mountain ranges are lettered with their names, and sea serpents, whales and carracks swim in the open ocean; a title cartouche held by cherubs names your realm and the year in the sheet's corner, a compass rose is printed in the widest sea, a scale of miles in the lower corner, and the blank places read Terra Incognita
- Realms are lettered across their lands in spaced capitals; their borders are a wash of their colour inside a dotted line; the sheet is browned at its edges and creased where it was folded
- A village grows into a market town (or a harbour town on the coast), a great walled city at ten people, and a capital is a star fortress; town names are on parchment ribbons
- Units stand on painted wargame bases with a pennant in their realm's colour and turn to face the way they marched; from far off they show as wooden wargame blocks marked infantry, horse, guns or ships; regiment counts are pressed into wax seals
- Fields where a regiment fell are marked on the chart with crossed swords and the year, as the old maps marked their battles (and they stay marked)
- The route of march is a red dashed line with an arrowhead, roads are double-ruled, strength and morale are little ink-ruled gauges, and map messages are lettered in ink
- Every icon, every event picture, every ruler's portrait and the pictures behind the menu are hand-coloured engravings; End Turn is a wax-red button; the tech tree is a set of parchment cards; all panels are leather in gilt frames
- The chart lies on a leather desk, throwing a soft shadow, with the chartmaker's brass dividers and magnifying glass beside it; a town's garrison stands at its gate so the town can still be seen
- Deep water is hatched in fine level lines and shaded slopes in short strokes, as a copperplate engraver works; roads cross rivers on little stone bridges and a fortified town's walls are a bastioned trace; shallows are stippled off every shore, rivers snake and widen toward the sea, hills are shaded molehills, and wonders of nature are named beneath them; a siege is drawn as a ring of earthworks in red ink, and newly found land is inked in out of the blank sheet
- The city and unit panels are headed by the town's or regiment's own engraving; research is crowned by a gloria of gilt rays; the turn is announced with the season and the year in Roman numerals; a new game opens on the whole chart lying on the desk and leans in to your capital, and a big world opens with the chartmaker at work
- A wind head puffs from the sheet's corner and a key to its marks (Explicatio Notarum) sits in another; a new town, or one that changes hands, is stamped with its realm's wax seal; figures step along as they march, cast long shadows to the south-east (towns and works too) and lean a little away from the middle of the view, like miniatures on a table; your marches this turn are pricked out in dots
- Nine more event engravings (plague, storm, fire, a comet, a royal wedding, pilgrims at the cathedral, wolves in the forest, conspirators, brigands), so events show fitting pictures; the frame is numbered in degrees and the sheet signed in its foot margin; the country round a town is under the plough and settled land is dotted with little churches; a town in danger is ringed in red ink; ruler portraits are engraved miniatures in oval gilt frames; the event log is a page of the chronicle in ink on parchment; plans are pencilled on the chart, and a gunner's targets are marked with red cross-hairs
- The blank sheet is smoke-browned vellum lying on a desk, with older sheets of the survey askew beneath it, an inkwell and quill and a seal with its wax beside it, and a reading glass that shows the leather under it magnified; the chart is printed on laid paper, the land you've charted casts a soft shadow onto the blank sheet, and a small world lies in the middle of the desk
- Powder smoke, hearth smoke and burning towns are billowed clouds inked round and hatched on their shaded side, as the battle prints drew them, and a musket's flash is struck out in fine rays; borders are laid on in watercolour fading inward from the line, and a unit's reach is pencilled as a staff officer marks a day's march
- The menu's title is set on a tooled-leather board in gilt, and the minimap is drawn on the same blank vellum; names on the chart wait until the land under both their ends is known, and a new game no longer shows a glimpse of the last one's land
- The map redraws far faster: a new turn or season recolours the sheet in a fraction of the time, and panning stays smooth at every zoom
Beta 12.1
Hard Choices
- Every one of the 120 events has been rebalanced: each answer now has its own cost, risk or later consequence, no single answer is clearly best, and "do nothing" is never free
- New kinds of answer: gambles (a stated chance of something going wrong, or right) and investments that pay off a few turns later (crop rotation leaves fields fallow now and brings in a big harvest in five turns). Both are shown on the card, and the chronicle tells you when they come true
- The cards now show everything a choice does: the change in noble opinion that comes with legitimacy, deaths at court, recruits. Gains grow with your realm just as costs always did
- Some answers can now change fate: the right physicians may save your consort from the palace plague, and a general can be hired into your service
Beta 12.0
The Old World
- The map is an engraved, hand-coloured atlas sheet: relief shaded hills and mountain ranges, inked coasts with lines of water out to sea, woods drawn tree by tree, hatched hills and marsh reeds, all on aged paper inside a ruled border
- The known world fades softly into the blank vellum, where rhumb lines run out from wind-roses as on a portolan chart; land you are not watching is dimmed rather than blacked out
- The seasons recolour the whole sheet: green spring, gold summer, russet autumn, and snow with frozen shallows in winter
- Towns, farms, mines, mills, ports and wonders are little engraved vignettes, and every unit is an engraved figure
- Panels are tooled leather in gilt frames; the ground a unit can reach is one wash ruled round its edge
Beta 11.2
The Pixel Map, Sharpened
- The map is back to its bright pixel look, redrawn at twice the detail: shaded hexes, grass tufts and flowers, ripples on the water and outlined trees and buildings
- Mountains are pixel peaks with snowy tops and hills are green mounds; towns are drawn as before, with snow on their roofs in winter and captured colours flying beside the capital's church
- Soldiers, horsemen, guns and ships are small pixel figures to match the map, each standing inside its own hex
- No more emoji anywhere: the animals on the map, city-site flags, markers and messages are all drawn as painted icons
Beta 11.1
Starving Garrisons
- Troops holding a town besieged for four turns or more are weakened by hunger: blows against them land 15% harder, and the attack preview says so
Beta 11.0
Terms from the Starving
- A rival whose town is starving under your siege sues for peace (you are asked in Kingdoms, as with any offer); rivals starving each other ask for terms too
Beta 10.9
Fixes
- Siege rings, trampled fields and siege tooltips no longer show for a rival's town hidden in fog (they gave away troops you couldn't see)
- Wiping out a rival now closes the chronicle of that war too, as a conquest
- The cut-road warning is no longer repeated after loading a game, is given once a siege lifts with the road still cut, and starts afresh for a captured town
- A rival with no free shore no longer keeps buying stone for a harbour it cannot build
Beta 10.8
Polish
- The peace summary counts the colours taken and lost in the war
- Siege rings are hidden at the furthest zoom, where they cluttered the overview
Beta 10.7
Starved Out
- A town under siege for four turns running begins to starve: it loses one family to hunger every three turns (never the last) until the siege is lifted. The town tooltip counts the turns of siege
Beta 10.6
Trophies
- The latest colours a realm has taken hang over its capital as a row of small flags, each in the colours of the realm it was taken from
Beta 10.5
Reading the War from the Map
- Hovering over a town tells you if it is besieged, blockaded or cut off, and how many of its tiles the enemy holds; hovering over a held field names the town it is lost to
- The road tooltip says that a road costs one move per step
Beta 10.4
Taking the Colours
- A regiment destroyed in battle may leave its colours on the field. Taking an enemy's colours raises your legitimacy a little and lowers theirs; losing your own does the reverse. The chronicle records each one
Beta 10.3
Laurels
- A regiment with three or more battle honours wears a gold laurel on the map (a brighter one from eight)
Beta 10.2
Battle Honours
- Every regiment keeps count of the enemies it has destroyed, attacking or holding its ground; hover over it to see its honours beside its name
Beta 10.1
The Reckoning of a War
- When you make peace, the chronicle sums up the war: how long the fighting lasted, how many regiments you lost and how many you destroyed, and whether it was a victorious or a hard-won peace
Beta 10.0
Towns Under Snow
- In winter the towns lie under a dusting of snow, thickest on the roofs
Beta 9.9
Hardship
- A town under siege grows restless (+1.5 discontent); one with enemy troops in its fields or its harbour blockaded a little (+0.5). Both show in the town's mood breakdown
Beta 9.8
Siege Lines
- Any town under siege that you can see, yours or a rival's, is ringed in orange, so you can tell at a glance which of your own sieges are holding
Beta 9.7
Cut Roads
- Enemy troops standing on a road cut it: the town at its end loses its trade with the capital until the road is clear, and you are told when one of yours is cut
- Markets in fields held by the enemy no longer earn their Banking or Merchants' Guild bonus
Beta 9.6
Siege Fixes
- A town you capture no longer inherits its old owner's siege (your own troops at its gates counted as besiegers for a turn, and you were told a siege had lifted)
- Driving the besiegers off during your turn frees the fields for that same turn's harvest; a siege carries over correctly when a game is loaded, without a repeated warning
- Starting a new game clears the old map's roads at once
Harbours
- Rivals who know Navigation send a worker to the shore to build a first harbour, and buy the stone for it if they are short
Beta 9.5
Blockades
- An enemy warship lying beside a port closes it: no trade or catch comes in from it, the town's fishing boats stay in, and you are told when a blockade begins and ends
Beta 9.4
Roads That Carry Armies
- A step along a road costs one move whatever the ground: through forest, over hills and across rivers (anyone's troops may use them, so mind your roads in wartime)
- Timber bridges are drawn where a road crosses a river
Beta 9.3
Frozen Rivers
- In winter the rivers freeze hard: troops behind a river lose its protection until the thaw (the tile tooltip says so)
Beta 9.2
Hearth Smoke
- In autumn and winter, pale smoke rises from the chimneys of every town, more of it from the larger towns
Beta 9.1
A Painted Map
- The map is hand-painted: meadows, forests, marsh, snowfields, rock, sea and ice, with painted farms, mines, mills, markets, ports and town houses
- Settlements are painted too: a village grows into a walled market town at 5 people, and capitals are star-fortress cities
- Mountains rise as painted peaks and hills roll; ruins, barbarian camps, redoubts, town landmarks and the wonders of nature are painted as well
Relief Columns
- Rival troops marching to a threatened town now strike the besiegers they find at its gates when the fight looks good, instead of standing beside them
Beta 9.0
Living Off the Land
- Troops standing in an enemy town's fields forage: each sends a little food home and its men recover a little strength every turn
- Fields held by the enemy are drawn trampled and stripped, with the rings of their campfires
Beta 8.9
Look
- Units on the map are painted soldiers, gunners and ships in place of round badges, ringed in their nation's colour
- The emoji across menus, panels and messages are replaced by painted icons; unit lists and the unit panel show each soldier
Sieges
- Enemy troops standing in a town's fields take their harvest: those fields bring in nothing while they stay (the city's yield breakdown shows what is lost)
- Two or more at its gates put the town under siege and cut its road trade; you are told when a siege begins and when it is lifted
Rivers
- Rivers no longer coil round flat country into a solid knot of river tiles (one town could have a river in every field); they run in a line and end where the ground stops falling
Beta 8.8
Towns Ablaze
- A town that has just been taken or sacked burns for a few turns: embers at its heart and columns of smoke leaning downwind, thinning as the fires die
Beta 8.7
Battle Honours
- The chronicle records your regiments' victories by name, such as "The 1st Regiment of Foot destroyed Austria's 3rd Regiment of Foot"
- Promotions now name the regiment that earned them
Beta 8.6
Towns Before Colonies
- Rivals send out settlers only from towns of three or more, so a food-rich realm no longer drains every town down to a single family
Beta 8.5
Fewer Freebies
- The largest maps hold at most 40 ancient ruins (there were a hundred, a little too much treasure lying about)
Beta 8.4
Roll of Honour
- When one of your regiments falls, the chronicle records it by name ("Lost: the 3rd Hussars")
Beta 8.3
Colours of the Regiments
- Every regiment carries a number and a name in the manner of the day, counted for each realm as it is raised: the 1st Regiment of Foot, the 3rd Hussars, the 2nd Battery of Horse Artillery. Hover a unit to see it
Beta 8.2
The Edge of the Known World
- The frontier of what you've explored is softly shaded, so your map fades into the unexplored chart instead of ending in a hard edge
Beta 8.1
Smoother Hands
- Moving the mouse while smoke or floating numbers are on screen no longer stacks up extra redraws (it could stutter badly after a battle)
- Lifting the last finger after a pinch-zoom no longer counts as a tap (it could select, move or attack)
- A sideways swipe doesn't zoom, and a trackpad's small nudges add up to one zoom step instead of each zooming a full step
- Keys held when the window loses focus (or pressed with Cmd/Ctrl) no longer leave the map panning on its own
- A long chain of planned moves or a long battle replay isn't cut off by a click; if something really is stuck, units are let go cleanly
- Resizing the window keeps the view in range; move previews no longer wrap round at the map's right edge
- Rivals resent a realm with 40% of the cities only once there are at least eight in the world (the first to found a second city was set upon by everyone)
Beta 8.0
Harbour Life
- Coastal towns keep fishing boats on the water beside them (one for a small place, two from 6 people), drawn up out of the ice in winter
Beta 7.9
Camp Burners
- Rival soldiers with nothing better to do (no foe near, no city to march on) go after raider camps near their towns instead of wandering, and burn any left unguarded
Beta 7.8
Mustering
- A new land unit with no room around its city musters inside the walls (up to three there), instead of waiting turn after turn with "No room to deploy"
Beta 7.7
The Race for Wonders
- Each wonder of nature has a marked city site beside it, so it is worth racing for, and your rivals now go after them
Beta 7.6
Tidier Borders
- A city's lands grow outward nearest-first into a compact shape, and natural growth reaches only so far: 2 tiles for a small town, 3 from 5 people, 4 from 10 (borders used to creep on for ever, one town ending with ninety tiles and swallowing the sites others might have settled). Bought tiles and Urban quarters can still push past it
- Games started or loaded without the New Game screen's barbarian settings use the same defaults it shows (they were harsher)
Beta 7.5
No Death Spirals
- A noble house that has risen in rebellion needs fifteen turns before it can rise again (a weak realm used to face a new rising every few turns and never recover)
- A realm at its lowest ebb (legitimacy under 15) slowly recovers, +0.5 a turn
Beta 7.4
Workers Keep Their Heads
- Automated workers, and your rivals', run for the nearest city of their realm when raiders or an enemy army come within two tiles, and won't take a job right beside the enemy (they used to be carried off one by one)
Beta 7.3
Growing Towns
- A big town spills over into the country round it: hamlets of houses appear on its neighbouring land at 8 people, more at 12 and 16
Beta 7.2
Border Works
- Rivals at war dig redoubts on the border facing their enemy
Fixes
- A city frees only an enemy's or raider's captive; a friendly worker or settler passing through is no longer taken
- A worker you give an order (a move, a Go To, a build or auto-explore) is taken off automation, so it doesn't wander back to spending your gold
- Rival settlers give up a site they can't get nearer to (across water or a closed border) and choose another, instead of stalling for twenty-five turns
- A rival city that gives up on a build no longer carries its finished work into the next one (units used to appear at once)
- Battle scars are left only where you could see the fighting
- Raider camps, ruins, wonders of nature and city sites never share a tile; a new game starts with no roads left over from the last
- Faster on big maps: science-lab counts are worked out once a turn
Beta 7.1
Weather
- Cloud shadows pass over the land and sea, drifting on with the wind from turn to turn
- The attack preview names a Redoubt's shelter, as it does a river crossing
Beta 7.0
Redoubts
- Workers can raise a Redoubt (15 stone, 10 wood, 3 turns) on open ground, hills, woods or marsh: an earthwork ring with a palisade and your pennant. A unit holding it takes 25% less damage, from blows and from fire alike
- Rivals weigh wonders of nature when choosing where to settle
Beta 6.9
Wonders of Nature
- Every map holds a few wonders of nature: the Great Falls (on a river), the Ancient Oak, the Crystal Peak, the Salt Marsh and the Sacred Grove. The city whose lands hold one draws its gifts (food, gold, science, stone, or legitimacy for the realm); the first time your people set eyes on one, you're rewarded. Hover one to see what it gives
Beta 6.8
Winter Ice & a Steadier Realm
- In winter the sea along every shore freezes over and rivers run icy pale
Fixes
- A realm whose legitimacy hits zero stays there until it earns it back (it used to spring back to 50 the next turn)
- A widowed ruler takes a new consort, so the line of heirs goes on; when a noble house's head dies, his own house picks the successor (two houses could end up sharing one head)
- Captured workers and scouts are held by the raiders, not sent to fight, and go free to whoever takes their camp
- Raider camps and rebellions each keep their own banner (a camp's fall could wipe out an unrelated rising)
- Wars with realms already destroyed no longer weary your cities
- The one-time boons of Vassalage and Divine Rule come once, not every time the law is swapped back in
- Tribes no longer carry an unseen court that aged, died and held elections
Beta 6.7
Generals from the Ranks
- A seasoned soldier (Veteran or better) who wins a fight may now and then see one of its officers raised to general, while the realm has fewer than two
- Hovering a tile tells you more: a river's food, gold and defence, ancient ruins, a recent battlefield, a road to the capital
- An afternoon light lies over the map: warm from the upper left, cooler toward the lower right
Beta 6.6
Workers at Work
- Automate workers (B, or the button on a worker's panel): it mends what raiders spoiled, improves your land and moves on to the next bare tile by itself each turn. It never fells a forest unasked, and Next Unit passes it by
- Workers, yours and your rivals', head for the nearest tile they can actually improve instead of wandering (rival lands now fill with farms and mines several times faster)
- Saves keep each city's militia cooldown (reloading used to raise a fresh militia every turn)
Beta 6.5
On the March
- Columns on the march raise dust at each step (horse more than foot), and ships leave a white wake
- In winter, units caught outside a city wear a ring of frost, so you can see who is suffering the cold
Beta 6.4
Better Lands
- Every map gets a like balance: about 30% sea and 9% snowy heights whatever the dice (one map could be a third mountains), with woods on about 45% of the lowland and more open plains for farms and markets
- A captive worker standing in a city is freed by its people; an undefended city calls up its militia even with a captive inside
- Rival realms short of everything buy steel or food on the market to rebuild, and in an emergency raise only soldiers they can actually pay for (a realm could sit for years on a cannon it could never afford)
- Fixed faint vertical stripes over the fog and borders when zoomed far out
Beta 6.3
Fords & Fields of Battle
- River crossings: a melee attack from off the river onto a defender standing on river land falls 15% lighter. The attack preview says so
- Where soldiers fall, the ground stays scorched and strewn with spent shot and wreckage for a few turns, fading as the land recovers
Beta 6.2
Rivers That Matter
- Every river tile in a city's lands gives +0.5 food and +0.5 gold (shown in the city's statistics), and rivals now prefer to settle by rivers
- A city that can't place a finished unit (every tile round it taken) no longer piles up production while it waits; a rival city boxed in by its own army builds a granary, walls or a factory instead
- Rival treasuries sell surplus food on the market when they run short of gold
Beta 6.1
Fair Fights & a Truer Map
Combat fixes
- Formations and generals defend the right way round: Square really is +30% defence (it was taking 30% more damage), Line -15%, and a cautious general's +15% protects his men
- Ranged units fire at most two tiles away, and not after moving (dragoons excepted); they can no longer strike from four tiles off through a move order
- Units can't walk through other armies to reach the tiles behind them
- Rival artillery waits out its reload even when an enemy stands next to it
- When a city falls, only its civilians go over to the new owner; soldiers in its lands stay loyal
- Resting never lowers morale (a line abroad used to bleed it away), and law-raised morale ceilings are kept
- The combat preview, and the rivals' judgement of a fight, count the counter-blow as it really falls
Map
- Your units that can still act this turn wear a small gold pip
- Faster drawing: fog, borders' tint and seasons cost far less when zoomed out on a big map
Beta 6.0
Landmarks & Mixed Armies
- Towns show what they've built: a granary and its silo, a factory with a smoking chimney, and a landmark for each wonder (the Library's dome, the Cathedral's towers, the Arsenal and its cannon, the gilded Guildhall, the War College colonnade)
- Rival armies are mixed: foot, horse and guns, with artillery kept to about a quarter (late-game rivals used to field nothing but field guns)
- Rival workers build a first harbour once they know Navigation, so they can put ships to sea
- Empire overview (O, or the new top-bar button): every city in one table with its people, mood, spare food, gold, science, what it's building and who guards it; click one to go there
- The minimap is larger and sharp, fills its frame edge to edge (a quarter of it stood empty), shows cities as ringed dots and the view as a true-sized frame, and a click lands where you clicked
- A unit's health and morale show as bars, and its moves, sight, attack and the ground's defence as chips
- City names are banners in the realm's colours under each town, with its size, a star for a capital, a red count while it's being taken, and what it has built
- Volume sliders in Options for the music, the land's own sounds (birds, towns, marching) and the effects, kept between games
- Portraits: rulers and consorts are painted in the court dress of their own people, in the Court, on each realm's card in Kingdoms, at a first meeting, on a declaration of war (over a war camp) and among the candidates of an election
Beta 5.9
Ruins & Raiders
- Ancient ruins lie scattered across the wild land. The first unit of any realm to reach them finds something: a strongbox of gold, scholars' notes for your research, a sealed granary, an old map of the country round about, or a veterans' cache of arms
- Barbarian camps are drawn as camps: hide tents round a fire, a ring of stakes and a ragged black banner
- Raiders sack any town of three or more people (as they do a capital) instead of burning it down; only small villages can still be razed
- A soft vignette frames the map
- Events have a painted scene over them (the court, a camp, the countryside, a market, a harbour, a mine, envoys, a study), and each answer's costs and gains show as red and green chips
- Victory and defeat are painted too; a score result at turn 200 can be played on past with Keep Playing
Beta 5.8
Seasons, Sentries & Settlers
- Seasons show on the land: snow lies in winter, the woods turn gold in autumn, spring greens
- Enemies at the gates: a city with a hostile army within three tiles is ringed in red, and you're warned when the danger appears
- Settlers now cost 30 food and one citizen from the city that trains them (it needs at least 2). A city training them pauses its growth only once it can spare them
- Rival settlers head for the site they chose instead of wandering, and realms with food to spare found more cities
- New keys: K Kingdoms, + / - zoom, Z wakes a fortified unit (W only pans the map now, and never cancels a worker's build)
Fixes
- Workers mid-build and fortified units can't be sent off with planning orders or auto-explore (a worker could carry its build to another tile)
- Escape on the tech tree just closes it; game keys no longer act behind it or on the title screen
- A war started by caught spies cancels open borders and other agreements; the gold counter updates after spying or a mapping deal
- Upgrading a unit drops a formation the new unit can't use (a column hussar made a lancer kept +2 moves)
- A worker's "Buy Adjacent Tile" really is adjacent to the worker
- Markets being built count toward the next one's price, and cancelling a build refunds what was paid
Screens
- Tech tree laid out across the screen in three bands; hover a tech to light the road to it; click a locked one to make it your goal, and the techs on the way are studied in turn. Progress on a tech is kept when you switch away and back
- Kingdoms: each realm a card with an opinion bar, its army against yours, what it asks of you, your actions in one row and your pacts as chips
- The top bar fits a laptop: End Turn and the buttons at its right end no longer run off the screen
- The tutorial lights up what each card describes, and the research prompt waits until it's done
- Rulers, heirs and the great families have names from their own nation (twelve name lists, French at the French court and so on)
- City yields as coloured chips; dark scrollbars throughout
Beta 5.7
Roads, Shores & Painted Borders
- Roads: each city is joined to its capital by a road over land that doesn't cross a rival's territory. A city on the road earns +2 gold in trade (shown in its statistics); roads redraw as cities are founded or lost
- Borders are drawn like a painted map: dark ink beneath, the realm's colour, a light inner edge. The territory tint is one even wash instead of a grid
- The sea has surf along every shore and wave marks on open water
- Rivers are drawn as winding streams that follow the way the water runs, with tributaries joining and a mouth at the sea (older saves work out their rivers' flow when loaded)
- Battle replays only show fights you can see or take part in, skip the camera pan when the fight is already on screen, and play briskly on a busy turn
Beta 5.6
Towns, Trade & Militia
- Every city is drawn as a little town that grows with its people: a church and your flag over the capital, a ring wall once fortified
- Units are lit, brass-rimmed medallions standing on their own shadow
- The fog of war is one even shade instead of a grid of dark hex edges
- Market (top bar or M): sell surplus food, wood, stone, steel or gunpowder for gold, or buy what you lack. Prices slide as you trade and settle again next turn. Rival treasuries use it too
- An undefended city with an enemy at its gates calls up a militia (once every ten turns)
- Cities build faster as they grow, instead of every city working at the same pace
- Rivals short of gold build workers first and aim at units they can afford, rather than sitting empty-handed
- Muskets, rifles and cannon fire with a flash and a bank of drifting powder smoke; blows raise dust where they land
- An event you can't afford any answer to can now be declined (a little legitimacy lost) instead of locking the game
- Research picks up: every city's townsfolk add science (1 + 0.4 per citizen), so a growing realm reaches new techs every ten or so turns instead of every forty
- Fixed a battle replay that could wait forever when the camera was asked to pan twice at once
Beta 5.5
Living Rivals, Hungry Cities & a Sharper Map
Economy & AI
- Cities grow only when they make more food than they eat; with the stores empty, a starving city can lose a citizen. The city panel shows the real food balance
- A city training a Settler stops growing while it saves the food
- AI rivals expand again: they found new cities instead of sitting on one, and stop waiting forever on builds they can't pay for
- Barbarians sack a capital instead of razing it: they carry off gold and food, burn a building and leave
Diplomacy
- Seek Peace is now an offer the other side weighs (armies and goodwill); an accepted peace holds for ten turns
- An AI ally can't join a war on you during a treaty, and you're told when one does
- Barbarian raids no longer count as "being at war" when asking for agreements
Map & menus
- Sharp on Retina and other high-density screens
- Unexplored land is a dark old chart; the camera can centre any tile, including the map's edges, and dragging glides
- Starting capitals sit away from the map's edge with land to work
- New painted menu backdrops; the menu fits a phone
Fixes
- Rushed units pay their materials and need room to stand; the game stops cleanly at victory or defeat; loading a save no longer shows the last game's map; new games start in spring; the Engineers law's extra worker step applies to every worker; hex distances, promotions, research overflow and many smaller fixes
Beta 5.4
Old World — City Loyalty, Laws & Statistics Panel
City Loyalty (Old World-style)
- Discontent vs Order replaces the old jobs-only mood. Cities track foreign culture, recent conquest, distance from capital, war weariness, low legitimacy, winter, slavery, and cruel rulers as discontent — countered by fortifications, cathedrals, granaries, garrisons, capital status, charismatic rulers, high legitimacy, and Tyranny
- Six mood tiers: Loyal (+10% production, faster growth) → Content → Uneasy → Unhappy → Furious → Rebellious (foreign-cultured cities can flip back to their original owner; native cities spawn rebel barbarians)
- When a city flips back via rebellion, the capital is reassigned, foreign garrison troops are killed, and non-combat units defect — matching capture rules
- Captured cities remember their original culture forever; re-conquest, garrisoning, or cathedrals can suppress unrest but not erase it
- City panel now shows the full discontent / order breakdown inline so you can see what is destabilising a city at a glance

Laws of the Realm — press L or click the new top-bar Laws button
- Six paired law slots inspired by Old World. First adoption in a category costs 1 order; switching costs 1 order + 60 gold:
  • Governance: Centralization (+1 order, +1 legitimacy/turn) vs Vassalage (+10 family opinion, +10% building production, halved legitimacy gains)
  • Labor: Slavery (+25% production, +1 discontent/city, family opinion drain) vs Freedom (+1 science & +1 food per city, +20% growth)
  • Culture: Epic Poetry (+1 legitimacy/turn, +3 morale, capital order) vs Divine Rule (+15 legitimacy on adoption, family opinion drift, but unbeliever discontent)
  • Order [needs Banking]: Tyranny (cities -2 discontent, family opinion drain, cheaper espionage) vs Constitution (rush -25%, +0.5 legitimacy + 0.5 family opinion/turn)
  • Military [needs Military Leadership]: Limitanei (-50% maintenance, -1 ATK, +1 free unit/city) vs Standing Army (+1 ATK, +50% maintenance, +2 starting XP)
  • Crafts [needs Engineering]: Engineers (+1 worker move, +20% production, cheaper wonders) vs Stonecutters (-25% stone/wood for buildings, fortifications give extra order)
- Adopting Vassalage instantly grants all your noble families +10 opinion; Divine Rule grants +15 legitimacy

City Statistics Panel — click the 📊 Statistics button on any city panel
- Production / turn as segmented pip bars for each resource (food, gold, wood, stone, steel, science, gunpowder), each with its own cap. Bars fill toward the cap and glow with a ★ MAX badge when reached or exceeded
- Public Mood shown as a split pip bar with red Discontent on the left, green Order on the right, plus per-factor bars for every contributing pressure or support
- Population shown as a citizen bar that lights up with a ★ FULL badge when the city hits its job cap
- Every yield breakdown lists the source: city center, tile improvements, banking, wonders, ruler bonuses, season multiplier, and active laws

Compatibility
- Saves are forward-compatible: existing cities are treated as native (originalNationId = current owner) and existing nations start with no laws adopted

- 3rd caught espionage now provokes an immediate war declaration with explicit warning
- Production overflow from rushed or factory builds now carries into the next queued item
- End-game score breakdown now matches the displayed total
- Settler "Found City" pending name no longer leaks across unit selection; F-shortcut now checks the same conditions as the button

Beta 12.2
The Atlas, Finished
- Snow drifts down over the map in winter and leaves blow across it in autumn; mountains rise in shaded relief and throw their shadows across the plains below; rivers start as fine lines in the hills and swell as streams join them on the way to the sea; pine woods grow in the north and under the mountains
- Seas, lakes and mountain ranges are lettered with their names, and sea serpents, whales and carracks swim in the open ocean; a title cartouche held by cherubs names your realm and the year in the sheet's corner, a compass rose is printed in the widest sea, a scale of miles in the lower corner, and the blank places read Terra Incognita
- Realms are lettered across their lands in spaced capitals; their borders are a wash of their colour inside a dotted line; the sheet is browned at its edges and creased where it was folded
- A village grows into a market town (or a harbour town on the coast), a great walled city at ten people, and a capital is a star fortress; town names are on parchment ribbons
- Units stand on painted wargame bases with a pennant in their realm's colour and turn to face the way they marched; from far off they show as wooden wargame blocks marked infantry, horse, guns or ships; regiment counts are pressed into wax seals
- Fields where a regiment fell are marked on the chart with crossed swords and the year, as the old maps marked their battles (and they stay marked)
- The route of march is a red dashed line with an arrowhead, roads are double-ruled, strength and morale are little ink-ruled gauges, and map messages are lettered in ink
- Every icon, every event picture, every ruler's portrait and the pictures behind the menu are hand-coloured engravings; End Turn is a wax-red button; the tech tree is a set of parchment cards; all panels are leather in gilt frames
- The chart lies on a leather desk, throwing a soft shadow, with the chartmaker's brass dividers and magnifying glass beside it; a town's garrison stands at its gate so the town can still be seen
- Deep water is hatched in fine level lines and shaded slopes in short strokes, as a copperplate engraver works; roads cross rivers on little stone bridges and a fortified town's walls are a bastioned trace; shallows are stippled off every shore, rivers snake and widen toward the sea, hills are shaded molehills, and wonders of nature are named beneath them; a siege is drawn as a ring of earthworks in red ink, and newly found land is inked in out of the blank sheet
- The city and unit panels are headed by the town's or regiment's own engraving; research is crowned by a gloria of gilt rays; the turn is announced with the season and the year in Roman numerals; a new game opens on the whole chart lying on the desk and leans in to your capital, and a big world opens with the chartmaker at work
- A wind head puffs from the sheet's corner and a key to its marks (Explicatio Notarum) sits in another; a new town, or one that changes hands, is stamped with its realm's wax seal; figures step along as they march, cast long shadows to the south-east (towns and works too) and lean a little away from the middle of the view, like miniatures on a table; your marches this turn are pricked out in dots
- Nine more event engravings (plague, storm, fire, a comet, a royal wedding, pilgrims at the cathedral, wolves in the forest, conspirators, brigands), so events show fitting pictures; the frame is numbered in degrees and the sheet signed in its foot margin; the country round a town is under the plough and settled land is dotted with little churches; a town in danger is ringed in red ink; ruler portraits are engraved miniatures in oval gilt frames; the event log is a page of the chronicle in ink on parchment; plans are pencilled on the chart, and a gunner's targets are marked with red cross-hairs
- The blank sheet is smoke-browned vellum lying on a desk, with older sheets of the survey askew beneath it, an inkwell and quill and a seal with its wax beside it, and a reading glass that shows the leather under it magnified; the chart is printed on laid paper, the land you've charted casts a soft shadow onto the blank sheet, and a small world lies in the middle of the desk
- Powder smoke, hearth smoke and burning towns are billowed clouds inked round and hatched on their shaded side, as the battle prints drew them, and a musket's flash is struck out in fine rays; borders are laid on in watercolour fading inward from the line, and a unit's reach is pencilled as a staff officer marks a day's march
- The menu's title is set on a tooled-leather board in gilt, and the minimap is drawn on the same blank vellum; names on the chart wait until the land under both their ends is known, and a new game no longer shows a glimpse of the last one's land
- The map redraws far faster: a new turn or season recolours the sheet in a fraction of the time, and panning stays smooth at every zoom
Beta 12.1
Hard Choices
- Every one of the 120 events has been rebalanced: each answer now has its own cost, risk or later consequence, no single answer is clearly best, and "do nothing" is never free
- New kinds of answer: gambles (a stated chance of something going wrong, or right) and investments that pay off a few turns later (crop rotation leaves fields fallow now and brings in a big harvest in five turns). Both are shown on the card, and the chronicle tells you when they come true
- The cards now show everything a choice does: the change in noble opinion that comes with legitimacy, deaths at court, recruits. Gains grow with your realm just as costs always did
- Some answers can now change fate: the right physicians may save your consort from the palace plague, and a general can be hired into your service
Beta 12.0
The Old World
- The map is an engraved, hand-coloured atlas sheet: relief shaded hills and mountain ranges, inked coasts with lines of water out to sea, woods drawn tree by tree, hatched hills and marsh reeds, all on aged paper inside a ruled border
- The known world fades softly into the blank vellum, where rhumb lines run out from wind-roses as on a portolan chart; land you are not watching is dimmed rather than blacked out
- The seasons recolour the whole sheet: green spring, gold summer, russet autumn, and snow with frozen shallows in winter
- Towns, farms, mines, mills, ports and wonders are little engraved vignettes, and every unit is an engraved figure
- Panels are tooled leather in gilt frames; the ground a unit can reach is one wash ruled round its edge
Beta 11.2
The Pixel Map, Sharpened
- The map is back to its bright pixel look, redrawn at twice the detail: shaded hexes, grass tufts and flowers, ripples on the water and outlined trees and buildings
- Mountains are pixel peaks with snowy tops and hills are green mounds; towns are drawn as before, with snow on their roofs in winter and captured colours flying beside the capital's church
- Soldiers, horsemen, guns and ships are small pixel figures to match the map, each standing inside its own hex
- No more emoji anywhere: the animals on the map, city-site flags, markers and messages are all drawn as painted icons
Beta 11.1
Starving Garrisons
- Troops holding a town besieged for four turns or more are weakened by hunger: blows against them land 15% harder, and the attack preview says so
Beta 11.0
Terms from the Starving
- A rival whose town is starving under your siege sues for peace (you are asked in Kingdoms, as with any offer); rivals starving each other ask for terms too

Beta 10.4
Taking the Colours
- A regiment destroyed in battle may leave its colours on the field. Taking an enemy's colours raises your legitimacy a little and lowers theirs; losing your own does the reverse. The chronicle records each one
Beta 10.3
Laurels
- A regiment with three or more battle honours wears a gold laurel on the map (a brighter one from eight)
Beta 10.2
Battle Honours
- Every regiment keeps count of the enemies it has destroyed, attacking or holding its ground; hover over it to see its honours beside its name
Beta 10.1
The Reckoning of a War
- When you make peace, the chronicle sums up the war: how long the fighting lasted, how many regiments you lost and how many you destroyed, and whether it was a victorious or a hard-won peace
Beta 10.0
Towns Under Snow
- In winter the towns lie under a dusting of snow, thickest on the roofs
Beta 9.9
Hardship
- A town under siege grows restless (+1.5 discontent); one with enemy troops in its fields or its harbour blockaded a little (+0.5). Both show in the town's mood breakdown
Beta 9.8
Siege Lines
- Any town under siege that you can see, yours or a rival's, is ringed in orange, so you can tell at a glance which of your own sieges are holding
Beta 9.7
Cut Roads
- Enemy troops standing on a road cut it: the town at its end loses its trade with the capital until the road is clear, and you are told when one of yours is cut
- Markets in fields held by the enemy no longer earn their Banking or Merchants' Guild bonus
Beta 9.6
Siege Fixes
- A town you capture no longer inherits its old owner's siege (your own troops at its gates counted as besiegers for a turn, and you were told a siege had lifted)
- Driving the besiegers off during your turn frees the fields for that same turn's harvest; a siege carries over correctly when a game is loaded, without a repeated warning
- Starting a new game clears the old map's roads at once
Harbours
- Rivals who know Navigation send a worker to the shore to build a first harbour, and buy the stone for it if they are short
Beta 9.5
Blockades
- An enemy warship lying beside a port closes it: no trade or catch comes in from it, the town's fishing boats stay in, and you are told when a blockade begins and ends
Beta 9.4
Roads That Carry Armies
- A step along a road costs one move whatever the ground: through forest, over hills and across rivers (anyone's troops may use them, so mind your roads in wartime)
- Timber bridges are drawn where a road crosses a river
Beta 9.3
Frozen Rivers
- In winter the rivers freeze hard: troops behind a river lose its protection until the thaw (the tile tooltip says so)
Beta 9.2
Hearth Smoke
- In autumn and winter, pale smoke rises from the chimneys of every town, more of it from the larger towns
Beta 9.1
A Painted Map
- The map is hand-painted: meadows, forests, marsh, snowfields, rock, sea and ice, with painted farms, mines, mills, markets, ports and town houses
- Settlements are painted too: a village grows into a walled market town at 5 people, and capitals are star-fortress cities
- Mountains rise as painted peaks and hills roll; ruins, barbarian camps, redoubts, town landmarks and the wonders of nature are painted as well
Relief Columns
- Rival troops marching to a threatened town now strike the besiegers they find at its gates when the fight looks good, instead of standing beside them
Beta 9.0
Living Off the Land
- Troops standing in an enemy town's fields forage: each sends a little food home and its men recover a little strength every turn
- Fields held by the enemy are drawn trampled and stripped, with the rings of their campfires
Beta 8.9
Look
- Units on the map are painted soldiers, gunners and ships in place of round badges, ringed in their nation's colour
- The emoji across menus, panels and messages are replaced by painted icons; unit lists and the unit panel show each soldier
Sieges
- Enemy troops standing in a town's fields take their harvest: those fields bring in nothing while they stay (the city's yield breakdown shows what is lost)
- Two or more at its gates put the town under siege and cut its road trade; you are told when a siege begins and when it is lifted
Rivers
- Rivers no longer coil round flat country into a solid knot of river tiles (one town could have a river in every field); they run in a line and end where the ground stops falling
Beta 8.8
Towns Ablaze
- A town that has just been taken or sacked burns for a few turns: embers at its heart and columns of smoke leaning downwind, thinning as the fires die
Beta 8.7
Battle Honours
- The chronicle records your regiments' victories by name, such as "The 1st Regiment of Foot destroyed Austria's 3rd Regiment of Foot"
- Promotions now name the regiment that earned them
Beta 8.6
Towns Before Colonies
- Rivals send out settlers only from towns of three or more, so a food-rich realm no longer drains every town down to a single family
Beta 8.5
Fewer Freebies
- The largest maps hold at most 40 ancient ruins (there were a hundred, a little too much treasure lying about)
Beta 8.4
Roll of Honour
- When one of your regiments falls, the chronicle records it by name ("Lost: the 3rd Hussars")
Beta 8.3
Colours of the Regiments
- Every regiment carries a number and a name in the manner of the day, counted for each realm as it is raised: the 1st Regiment of Foot, the 3rd Hussars, the 2nd Battery of Horse Artillery. Hover a unit to see it
Beta 8.2
The Edge of the Known World
- The frontier of what you've explored is softly shaded, so your map fades into the unexplored chart instead of ending in a hard edge
Beta 8.1
Smoother Hands
- Moving the mouse while smoke or floating numbers are on screen no longer stacks up extra redraws (it could stutter badly after a battle)
- Lifting the last finger after a pinch-zoom no longer counts as a tap (it could select, move or attack)
- A sideways swipe doesn't zoom, and a trackpad's small nudges add up to one zoom step instead of each zooming a full step
- Keys held when the window loses focus (or pressed with Cmd/Ctrl) no longer leave the map panning on its own
- A long chain of planned moves or a long battle replay isn't cut off by a click; if something really is stuck, units are let go cleanly
- Resizing the window keeps the view in range; move previews no longer wrap round at the map's right edge
- Rivals resent a realm with 40% of the cities only once there are at least eight in the world (the first to found a second city was set upon by everyone)
Beta 8.0
Harbour Life
- Coastal towns keep fishing boats on the water beside them (one for a small place, two from 6 people), drawn up out of the ice in winter
Beta 7.9
Camp Burners
- Rival soldiers with nothing better to do (no foe near, no city to march on) go after raider camps near their towns instead of wandering, and burn any left unguarded
Beta 7.8
Mustering
- A new land unit with no room around its city musters inside the walls (up to three there), instead of waiting turn after turn with "No room to deploy"
Beta 7.7
The Race for Wonders
- Each wonder of nature has a marked city site beside it, so it is worth racing for, and your rivals now go after them
Beta 7.6
Tidier Borders
- A city's lands grow outward nearest-first into a compact shape, and natural growth reaches only so far: 2 tiles for a small town, 3 from 5 people, 4 from 10 (borders used to creep on for ever, one town ending with ninety tiles and swallowing the sites others might have settled). Bought tiles and Urban quarters can still push past it
- Games started or loaded without the New Game screen's barbarian settings use the same defaults it shows (they were harsher)
Beta 7.5
No Death Spirals
- A noble house that has risen in rebellion needs fifteen turns before it can rise again (a weak realm used to face a new rising every few turns and never recover)
- A realm at its lowest ebb (legitimacy under 15) slowly recovers, +0.5 a turn
Beta 7.4
Workers Keep Their Heads
- Automated workers, and your rivals', run for the nearest city of their realm when raiders or an enemy army come within two tiles, and won't take a job right beside the enemy (they used to be carried off one by one)
Beta 7.3
Growing Towns
- A big town spills over into the country round it: hamlets of houses appear on its neighbouring land at 8 people, more at 12 and 16
Beta 7.2
Border Works
- Rivals at war dig redoubts on the border facing their enemy
Fixes
- A city frees only an enemy's or raider's captive; a friendly worker or settler passing through is no longer taken
- A worker you give an order (a move, a Go To, a build or auto-explore) is taken off automation, so it doesn't wander back to spending your gold
- Rival settlers give up a site they can't get nearer to (across water or a closed border) and choose another, instead of stalling for twenty-five turns
- A rival city that gives up on a build no longer carries its finished work into the next one (units used to appear at once)
- Battle scars are left only where you could see the fighting
- Raider camps, ruins, wonders of nature and city sites never share a tile; a new game starts with no roads left over from the last
- Faster on big maps: science-lab counts are worked out once a turn
Beta 7.1
Weather
- Cloud shadows pass over the land and sea, drifting on with the wind from turn to turn
- The attack preview names a Redoubt's shelter, as it does a river crossing
Beta 7.0
Redoubts
- Workers can raise a Redoubt (15 stone, 10 wood, 3 turns) on open ground, hills, woods or marsh: an earthwork ring with a palisade and your pennant. A unit holding it takes 25% less damage, from blows and from fire alike
- Rivals weigh wonders of nature when choosing where to settle
Beta 6.9
Wonders of Nature
- Every map holds a few wonders of nature: the Great Falls (on a river), the Ancient Oak, the Crystal Peak, the Salt Marsh and the Sacred Grove. The city whose lands hold one draws its gifts (food, gold, science, stone, or legitimacy for the realm); the first time your people set eyes on one, you're rewarded. Hover one to see what it gives
Beta 6.8
Winter Ice & a Steadier Realm
- In winter the sea along every shore freezes over and rivers run icy pale
Fixes
- A realm whose legitimacy hits zero stays there until it earns it back (it used to spring back to 50 the next turn)
- A widowed ruler takes a new consort, so the line of heirs goes on; when a noble house's head dies, his own house picks the successor (two houses could end up sharing one head)
- Captured workers and scouts are held by the raiders, not sent to fight, and go free to whoever takes their camp
- Raider camps and rebellions each keep their own banner (a camp's fall could wipe out an unrelated rising)
- Wars with realms already destroyed no longer weary your cities
- The one-time boons of Vassalage and Divine Rule come once, not every time the law is swapped back in
- Tribes no longer carry an unseen court that aged, died and held elections
Beta 6.7
Generals from the Ranks
- A seasoned soldier (Veteran or better) who wins a fight may now and then see one of its officers raised to general, while the realm has fewer than two
- Hovering a tile tells you more: a river's food, gold and defence, ancient ruins, a recent battlefield, a road to the capital
- An afternoon light lies over the map: warm from the upper left, cooler toward the lower right
Beta 6.6
Workers at Work
- Automate workers (B, or the button on a worker's panel): it mends what raiders spoiled, improves your land and moves on to the next bare tile by itself each turn. It never fells a forest unasked, and Next Unit passes it by
- Workers, yours and your rivals', head for the nearest tile they can actually improve instead of wandering (rival lands now fill with farms and mines several times faster)
- Saves keep each city's militia cooldown (reloading used to raise a fresh militia every turn)
Beta 6.5
On the March
- Columns on the march raise dust at each step (horse more than foot), and ships leave a white wake
- In winter, units caught outside a city wear a ring of frost, so you can see who is suffering the cold
Beta 6.4
Better Lands
- Every map gets a like balance: about 30% sea and 9% snowy heights whatever the dice (one map could be a third mountains), with woods on about 45% of the lowland and more open plains for farms and markets
- A captive worker standing in a city is freed by its people; an undefended city calls up its militia even with a captive inside
- Rival realms short of everything buy steel or food on the market to rebuild, and in an emergency raise only soldiers they can actually pay for (a realm could sit for years on a cannon it could never afford)
- Fixed faint vertical stripes over the fog and borders when zoomed far out
Beta 6.3
Fords & Fields of Battle
- River crossings: a melee attack from off the river onto a defender standing on river land falls 15% lighter. The attack preview says so
- Where soldiers fall, the ground stays scorched and strewn with spent shot and wreckage for a few turns, fading as the land recovers
Beta 6.2
Rivers That Matter
- Every river tile in a city's lands gives +0.5 food and +0.5 gold (shown in the city's statistics), and rivals now prefer to settle by rivers
- A city that can't place a finished unit (every tile round it taken) no longer piles up production while it waits; a rival city boxed in by its own army builds a granary, walls or a factory instead
- Rival treasuries sell surplus food on the market when they run short of gold
Beta 6.1
Fair Fights & a Truer Map
Combat fixes
- Formations and generals defend the right way round: Square really is +30% defence (it was taking 30% more damage), Line -15%, and a cautious general's +15% protects his men
- Ranged units fire at most two tiles away, and not after moving (dragoons excepted); they can no longer strike from four tiles off through a move order
- Units can't walk through other armies to reach the tiles behind them
- Rival artillery waits out its reload even when an enemy stands next to it
- When a city falls, only its civilians go over to the new owner; soldiers in its lands stay loyal
- Resting never lowers morale (a line abroad used to bleed it away), and law-raised morale ceilings are kept
- The combat preview, and the rivals' judgement of a fight, count the counter-blow as it really falls
Map
- Your units that can still act this turn wear a small gold pip
- Faster drawing: fog, borders' tint and seasons cost far less when zoomed out on a big map
Beta 6.0
Landmarks & Mixed Armies
- Towns show what they've built: a granary and its silo, a factory with a smoking chimney, and a landmark for each wonder (the Library's dome, the Cathedral's towers, the Arsenal and its cannon, the gilded Guildhall, the War College colonnade)
- Rival armies are mixed: foot, horse and guns, with artillery kept to about a quarter (late-game rivals used to field nothing but field guns)
- Rival workers build a first harbour once they know Navigation, so they can put ships to sea
- Empire overview (O, or the new top-bar button): every city in one table with its people, mood, spare food, gold, science, what it's building and who guards it; click one to go there
- The minimap is larger and sharp, fills its frame edge to edge (a quarter of it stood empty), shows cities as ringed dots and the view as a true-sized frame, and a click lands where you clicked
- A unit's health and morale show as bars, and its moves, sight, attack and the ground's defence as chips
- City names are banners in the realm's colours under each town, with its size, a star for a capital, a red count while it's being taken, and what it has built
- Volume sliders in Options for the music, the land's own sounds (birds, towns, marching) and the effects, kept between games
- Portraits: rulers and consorts are painted in the court dress of their own people, in the Court, on each realm's card in Kingdoms, at a first meeting, on a declaration of war (over a war camp) and among the candidates of an election
Beta 5.9
Ruins & Raiders
- Ancient ruins lie scattered across the wild land. The first unit of any realm to reach them finds something: a strongbox of gold, scholars' notes for your research, a sealed granary, an old map of the country round about, or a veterans' cache of arms
- Barbarian camps are drawn as camps: hide tents round a fire, a ring of stakes and a ragged black banner
- Raiders sack any town of three or more people (as they do a capital) instead of burning it down; only small villages can still be razed
- A soft vignette frames the map
- Events have a painted scene over them (the court, a camp, the countryside, a market, a harbour, a mine, envoys, a study), and each answer's costs and gains show as red and green chips
- Victory and defeat are painted too; a score result at turn 200 can be played on past with Keep Playing
Beta 5.8
Seasons, Sentries & Settlers
- Seasons show on the land: snow lies in winter, the woods turn gold in autumn, spring greens
- Enemies at the gates: a city with a hostile army within three tiles is ringed in red, and you're warned when the danger appears
- Settlers now cost 30 food and one citizen from the city that trains them (it needs at least 2). A city training them pauses its growth only once it can spare them
- Rival settlers head for the site they chose instead of wandering, and realms with food to spare found more cities
- New keys: K Kingdoms, + / - zoom, Z wakes a fortified unit (W only pans the map now, and never cancels a worker's build)
Fixes
- Workers mid-build and fortified units can't be sent off with planning orders or auto-explore (a worker could carry its build to another tile)
- Escape on the tech tree just closes it; game keys no longer act behind it or on the title screen
- A war started by caught spies cancels open borders and other agreements; the gold counter updates after spying or a mapping deal
- Upgrading a unit drops a formation the new unit can't use (a column hussar made a lancer kept +2 moves)
- A worker's "Buy Adjacent Tile" really is adjacent to the worker
- Markets being built count toward the next one's price, and cancelling a build refunds what was paid
Screens
- Tech tree laid out across the screen in three bands; hover a tech to light the road to it; click a locked one to make it your goal, and the techs on the way are studied in turn. Progress on a tech is kept when you switch away and back
- Kingdoms: each realm a card with an opinion bar, its army against yours, what it asks of you, your actions in one row and your pacts as chips
- The top bar fits a laptop: End Turn and the buttons at its right end no longer run off the screen
- The tutorial lights up what each card describes, and the research prompt waits until it's done
- Rulers, heirs and the great families have names from their own nation (twelve name lists, French at the French court and so on)
- City yields as coloured chips; dark scrollbars throughout
Beta 5.7
Roads, Shores & Painted Borders
- Roads: each city is joined to its capital by a road over land that doesn't cross a rival's territory. A city on the road earns +2 gold in trade (shown in its statistics); roads redraw as cities are founded or lost
- Borders are drawn like a painted map: dark ink beneath, the realm's colour, a light inner edge. The territory tint is one even wash instead of a grid
- The sea has surf along every shore and wave marks on open water
- Rivers are drawn as winding streams that follow the way the water runs, with tributaries joining and a mouth at the sea (older saves work out their rivers' flow when loaded)
- Battle replays only show fights you can see or take part in, skip the camera pan when the fight is already on screen, and play briskly on a busy turn
Beta 5.6
Towns, Trade & Militia
- Every city is drawn as a little town that grows with its people: a church and your flag over the capital, a ring wall once fortified
- Units are lit, brass-rimmed medallions standing on their own shadow
- The fog of war is one even shade instead of a grid of dark hex edges
- Market (top bar or M): sell surplus food, wood, stone, steel or gunpowder for gold, or buy what you lack. Prices slide as you trade and settle again next turn. Rival treasuries use it too
- An undefended city with an enemy at its gates calls up a militia (once every ten turns)
- Cities build faster as they grow, instead of every city working at the same pace
- Rivals short of gold build workers first and aim at units they can afford, rather than sitting empty-handed
- Muskets, rifles and cannon fire with a flash and a bank of drifting powder smoke; blows raise dust where they land
- An event you can't afford any answer to can now be declined (a little legitimacy lost) instead of locking the game
- Research picks up: every city's townsfolk add science (1 + 0.4 per citizen), so a growing realm reaches new techs every ten or so turns instead of every forty
- Fixed a battle replay that could wait forever when the camera was asked to pan twice at once
Beta 5.5
Living Rivals, Hungry Cities & a Sharper Map
Economy & AI
- Cities grow only when they make more food than they eat; with the stores empty, a starving city can lose a citizen. The city panel shows the real food balance
- A city training a Settler stops growing while it saves the food
- AI rivals expand again: they found new cities instead of sitting on one, and stop waiting forever on builds they can't pay for
- Barbarians sack a capital instead of razing it: they carry off gold and food, burn a building and leave
Diplomacy
- Seek Peace is now an offer the other side weighs (armies and goodwill); an accepted peace holds for ten turns
- An AI ally can't join a war on you during a treaty, and you're told when one does
- Barbarian raids no longer count as "being at war" when asking for agreements
Map & menus
- Sharp on Retina and other high-density screens
- Unexplored land is a dark old chart; the camera can centre any tile, including the map's edges, and dragging glides
- Starting capitals sit away from the map's edge with land to work
- New painted menu backdrops; the menu fits a phone
Fixes
- Rushed units pay their materials and need room to stand; the game stops cleanly at victory or defeat; loading a save no longer shows the last game's map; new games start in spring; the Engineers law's extra worker step applies to every worker; hex distances, promotions, research overflow and many smaller fixes
Beta 5.4
Old World — City Loyalty, Laws & Statistics Panel
City Loyalty (Old World-style)
- Discontent vs Order replaces the old jobs-only mood. Cities track foreign culture, recent conquest, distance from capital, war weariness, low legitimacy, winter, slavery, and cruel rulers as discontent — countered by fortifications, cathedrals, granaries, garrisons, capital status, charismatic rulers, high legitimacy, and Tyranny
- Six mood tiers: Loyal (+10% production, faster growth) → Content → Uneasy → Unhappy → Furious → Rebellious (foreign-cultured cities can flip back to their original owner; native cities spawn rebel barbarians)
- When a city flips back via rebellion, the capital is reassigned, foreign garrison troops are killed, and non-combat units defect to the new owner — matching the existing capture rules
- Captured cities remember their original culture forever; re-conquest, garrisoning, or cathedrals can suppress unrest but not erase it
- City panel now shows the full discontent / order breakdown inline so you can see what is destabilising a city at a glance

Laws of the Realm — press L or click the new top-bar Laws button
- Six paired law slots inspired by Old World. First adoption in a category costs 1 order; switching costs 1 order + 60 gold:
  • Governance: Centralization (+1 order, +1 legitimacy/turn) vs Vassalage (+10 family opinion, +10% building production, halved legitimacy gains)
  • Labor: Slavery (+25% production, +1 discontent/city, family opinion drain) vs Freedom (+1 science & +1 food per city, +20% growth)
  • Culture: Epic Poetry (+1 legitimacy/turn, +3 morale, capital order) vs Divine Rule (+15 legitimacy on adoption, family opinion drift, but unbeliever discontent)
  • Order [needs Banking]: Tyranny (cities -2 discontent, family opinion drain, cheaper espionage) vs Constitution (rush -25%, +0.5 legitimacy + 0.5 family opinion/turn)
  • Military [needs Military Leadership]: Limitanei (-50% maintenance, -1 ATK, +1 free unit/city) vs Standing Army (+1 ATK, +50% maintenance, +2 starting XP)
  • Crafts [needs Engineering]: Engineers (+1 worker move, +20% production, cheaper wonders) vs Stonecutters (-25% stone/wood for buildings, fortifications give extra order)
- Adopting Vassalage instantly grants all your noble families +10 opinion; Divine Rule grants +15 legitimacy

City Statistics Panel — click the 📊 Statistics button on any city panel
- Production / turn as segmented pip bars for each resource (food, gold, wood, stone, steel, science, gunpowder), each with its own cap. Bars fill toward the cap and glow with a ★ MAX badge when reached or exceeded
- Public Mood shown as a split pip bar with red Discontent on the left, green Order on the right, plus per-factor bars for every contributing pressure or support
- Population shown as a citizen bar that lights up with a ★ FULL badge when the city hits its job cap
- Every yield breakdown lists the source: city center, tile improvements, banking, wonders, ruler bonuses, season multiplier, and active laws

Compatibility
- Saves are forward-compatible: existing cities are treated as native (originalNationId = current owner) and existing nations start with no laws adopted
Beta 5.0
Bug Fixes, Diplomacy & Hex Math
- End Turn (E) is now ignored when ESC menu, war declaration, or popups are open, and can no longer double-fire on rapid presses
- Combat-range highlight, AI threat detection, and city-spacing now use true hex distance (no more diamond ranges)
- Hex neighbor checks no longer leak across map edges
- Scouts no longer wander open ocean indefinitely after Shipbuilding
- River crossing penalty now applies in both directions
- Go-To now refuses unreachable destinations instead of silently consuming a turn
- Tribes and barbarians correctly start at war and will fight one another
- Multi-war eliminations credit the actual conqueror; eliminated nations' agreements are cleaned up
- Peace treaties now include a 10-turn cooldown to stop war/peace flapping
- Player-declared wars now drag War Alliance partners into the war
- AI disbands cheapest units when bankrupt instead of getting free gold; no longer queues already-built buildings
- 3rd caught espionage now provokes an immediate war declaration with explicit warning
- Production overflow from rushed or factory builds now carries into the next queued item
- End-game score breakdown now matches the displayed total
- Settler "Found City" pending name no longer leaks across unit selection; F-shortcut now checks the same conditions as the button
- Escape now blurs text inputs instead of closing menus while typing
- Renamed cities, ruler/character/family names, and tile annotations are now safely escaped in all panels
Beta 4.9
Bug Fixes & Stability
- Loaded saves now self-heal missing relations/loyalty data, preventing crashes during AI turns and combat
- Barbarian density slider set to 0 now actually disables barbarians instead of falling back to 40%
- Declaring war no longer crashes on saves that predate the loyalty system
- Fortify, formation change, chop, hunt, repair, and rest no longer waste an order when the action is a no-op
- Settling a city only consumes an order on confirm, not when opening the name dialog
- Mortars no longer fire grapeshot — AI ammo switching now respects each unit's allowed ammo types
- Killing an enemy no longer advances the attacker onto an already-occupied tile, preventing unit stacking
- Founding a city or spawning a tribe now keeps tile ownership and city ownedTiles in sync
- Set Ammo rejects ammo types the unit cannot actually load
Beta 4.8
Bug Fixes & Quality
- Game now plays fully offline; fonts and assets are bundled locally
- Cavalry charge bonus and "no ranged attack after moving" now correctly account for morale and general move bonuses
- Selected-unit reference no longer dangles when the unit dies, is captured by the AI, or its city is razed
- AI no longer walks onto tiles already occupied by enemy units
- Production queue rejects duplicate non-wonder buildings, preventing double-builds
- Loyalty values can now legitimately reach 0 instead of snapping back to 50
- Pressing W to wake a fortified unit (or arrow keys to cycle stacks) no longer also pans the camera
- Eliminated nations with no clear conqueror cleanly remove their orphan units
- Producing a building that no longer exists no longer locks the city in an infinite production loop
Beta 4.7
Diplomacy & AI
- AI nations can now refuse diplomatic requests based on ruler personality and context
- Cruel, martial, and reckless rulers are more likely to decline; diplomatic rulers are easier
- Nations at war refuse open borders and mapping agreements more often
- Powerful nations are less receptive when you approach from a position of weakness
- AI nations now seek war alliances with loyal AI allies when at war
- AI seeks peace when severely outmatched, not just when loyalty recovers
- AI prioritises weakly defended enemy cities over just the closest one
Beta 4.6
Diplomacy & AI
- AI nations now declare war on each other, not just the player
- Wars between AI nations are announced with a toast notification
- Animals show as small corner badges instead of large overlays on tiles
- Foreign units can no longer enter your borders without an open borders agreement
- Cancelling open borders now expels enemy units from your territory
Beta 4.5
AI
- AI nations now research technologies throughout the game
- All nations have a minimum science income so research always progresses
- Smarter AI tech priority: cavalry only with horses, military urgency during war, varied paths
- Friendly AI nations will move units to hunt barbarians threatening player cities and units
- Corrupt units with null/NaN HP are removed on game load and each turn start
Beta 4.4
Fixes
- Fixed ranged attacks dealing NaN damage, leaving targets alive with corrupt HP
- Fixed ranged units unable to attack after previous combat changes
Beta 4.3
Combat
- Artillery units now have 4-tile attack range (5 on hills)
- Melee units can now move and attack in the same turn
- Barbarian units no longer stack on the same tile

Options
- Auto Next Unit toggle: disable automatic camera jump to next available unit after each action
Beta 4.2
Diplomacy
- Mapping Agreement: spend 30 gold to mutually reveal both nations' borders (requires Cautious+ relations)
- Infiltrate: spend 50 gold to covertly reveal an enemy's borders — 25% chance of discovery and loyalty loss

Fixes
- Fixed black screen flash during camera pan caused by accumulated canvas transform
- Rush produce no longer charges unit resource costs on top of the gold fee
- Unit upgrade now works anywhere within a city's borders, not just on the city tile
- Upgrade button now shows the correct unit name (e.g. Musketeer instead of Gunpowder Infantry)
Beta 4.1
Planning Mode (Cartography tech)
- Queue move and attack orders for multiple units simultaneously — all execute at once when you press P again
- Threat map: hover any enemy unit to see its movement range highlighted in red
- Combat preview: while assigning an attack order, hover an enemy to see estimated strike and retaliation damage
- Queued orders shown as coloured arrows on the map (blue = move, red = attack)
- Tile annotation (colour + label) still available by clicking empty tiles in planning mode

Balance
- Production and building costs scale with city count: each additional city raises all costs by 20%

Events Overhaul
- 31 events expanded to 120 — 89 new events across 15 categories

Bug Fixes
- Fixed rebel nations accumulating orphaned families and characters in memory over time

Changes
- Scrapped premade map ideas for now — nation selection screen, preset geographic city positions, world map terrain overrides, tribal nations system, and World map size all removed

Bug Fixes

- Fixed E key triggering End Turn while typing in text inputs (empire name etc.)

- Fixed fleeing units retaining stuck animation state, causing visual between-tile glitch

Balance
- Default barbarian density reduced to 40% (was 60%)
- Seasons now cycle every turn (1 turn per season, 4 turns = 1 year)
- Swordsman Charge ability added: can move and attack in the same turn unless in Square formation

Map Generation

Seasons & Calendar

Smarter AI

Bug Fixes
